sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:143053
Court No. - 70

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 27050 of 2023
Applicant :- Sanjeeda

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ehtesham Akhtar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Ehtesham Akhtar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ghanshyma Mishra,
learned Brief Holder for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
246 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Loni, District Ghaziabad, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and her family members including husband of the deceased and according to the FIR, marriage of the deceased was performed with the son of the applicant about 5 years before and after marriage applicant and her family members tortured the deceased for want of dowry and on 8.3.2023 in the night when informant received information then he arrived at the house of the applicant and came to know that her daughter has been died.

Sanjeeda vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6081087/
1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother in law and entire allegation of demand of dowry and torture made against the applicant is false and baseless and actually deceased even after five years of her marriage could not conceive and therefore, she under depression committed suicide.
He further submitted that even her autopsy report shows that she died due to asphyxia as a result of hanging.
5. He further submitted that applicant is a lady and she is in jail in the present matter since 20.3.2023, therefore, she may be released on bail.

6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that daughter in law of the applicant died under abnormal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that applicant is mother in law and there is no specific allegation against her and autopsy report of the deceased suggests that she died due to hanging.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, daughter in law of the applicant died under abnormal circumstances within five years of her marriage in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but applicant is mother in law of the deceased and no specific allegation has been made against her.

Further, post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging, therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that as even after five years of her marriage, deceased could not conceive, therefore, she committed suicide cannot be completely ruled out, at this stage.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant who is mother in law of the deceased is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Sanjeeda, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless her personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

Sanjeeda vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6081087/
2 12.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
